questions.q: Explain the different emphases of the First and Second Five Year Plans.
answer: After Independence, India chose planned development through the Planning Commission, and the first two Five Year Plans had very different emphases.

answer.text: The First Five Year Plan, from 1951 to 1956, gave priority to agriculture, irrigation and the rehabilitation of refugees from Partition. It was based on the Harrod-Domar model, which stressed raising savings and investment. Building large dams, which Nehru called the temples of modern India, was central to it. The aim was to lift the country out of food shortage and rural poverty.

The Second Five Year Plan, from 1956 to 1961, shifted the emphasis to rapid industrialisation, especially heavy and machine-making industries in the public sector. It was based on the Mahalanobis model, prepared by the statistician P.C. Mahalanobis, in the belief that heavy industry would make the country self-reliant and lay the base for future growth.

answer: Thus the First Plan focused on agriculture, while the Second Plan turned decisively towards industry.
